reason: Picomatch through 4.0.7: a single-branch repeated extglob such as +(*) or +(*a) skips analyzeRepeatedExtglob and compiles to a regular expression that backtracks exponentially, so an attacker who can supply the glob pattern can block the event loop. highsea resolves picomatch 4.0.7 and 2.3.2 only through build and test tools (Expo's CLI and Metro config, Metro's file map, Jest, React Native's codegen, @parcel/watcher, Vite and tinyglobby, Fumadocs, anymatch), which reach the server image as peers of expo, never as the server's own dependencies, and which the running server never loads; Next's compiled copy compiles only the image patterns in next.config, and highsea sets none. No highsea code imports picomatch, micromatch, anymatch or minimatch, so no pattern ever comes from a request, a setting or a file name. The advisory names no fixed release, and 4.0.7 is the latest on 2026-11-17. Look again when a fixed release can be pinned.
